messages.author: 301fd2bd8107629a
messages.subject: Announcement: Support for SQL Server
parts:
Hi all,

I've got a bleeding edge extension of dplyr methods for MS SQL Server in RSQLServer. I've tested this on one of our SQL Servers and the key methods work (mostly). It's using the jTDS drivers so it should work with MS SQL Server version 8+ (i.e. MS SQL Server 2000 +). 

I would appreciate any further testing by other users of SQL Server, new issues for bugs and pull requests for any fixes / improvements. I am hoping to introduce a test harness soon.

To install:

devtools::install_github("imanuelcostigan/RSQLServer@feature/dplyr")

Thanks!

messages.author: 301fd2bd8107629a
messages.subject: Re: Announcement: Support for SQL Server
parts:
Hi,

The only thing you should need to do is install the package. jTDS is cross platform. Having said that I've only used / tested this on Windows.

In terms of your error, the connection string you are using is unnecessary. 

Here's a template using DBI using the exact parameter argument names and replace the text in <> with values of your DB instance (per what you had in the connection string):

> dbConnect(SQLServer(), server = <serverName>, database = <databaseName>, user = <user>, password = <password>) 

Here's a template using dplyr interface:

> src_sqlserver(server = <serverName>, database = <databaseName>, user = <user>, password = <password>)

Thanks.

messages.author: b7e4534e95c25299
messages.subject: Re: Announcement: Support for SQL Server
parts:
(Accidentally sent directly—posting here for posterity) 

Ah, my mistake with how I had formatted the arguments. I’ve reformatted them as you’ve described them, but it appears Java is unable to locate the class:
> dbConnect(SQLServer(), server = <serverName>, database = <databaseName>, user = <user>, password = <password>)

Error in is(object, Cl) : 
  error in evaluating the argument 'drv' in selecting a method for function 'dbConnect': Error in .jfindClass(as.character(driverClass)[1]) : class not found

Even when the RSQLServer package is specified, it runs into the same error:

> RSQLServer::SQLServer()
Error in .jfindClass(as.character(driverClass)[1]) : class not found

How are you locating the jTDS driver? Speaking off the cuff here, but maybe it’s the difference in filesystem formatting between Windows and OS X/*nix systems? (e.g. \ vs / and their respective escapes.) Forgive me if I’m leaping to conclusions, but I’ve found the following pattern useful when relying on external dependencies across platforms: 

> if(Sys.info()['sysname'] == "Darwin"){
  JDBC("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver",
       "~/Downloads/sqljdbc_4.0/enu/sqljdbc4.jar")
} else if(Sys.info()['sysname'] == "Windows"){
  JDBC("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver",
            "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft JDBC Driver 4.0 for SQL Server\\sqljdbc_4.0\\enu\\sqljdbc4.jar")
} else {
  error("Sorry: your platform is not currently supported.")
}

The only thing you should need to do is install the package. jTDS is cross platform. Having said that I've only used / tested this on Windows.

In terms of your error, the connection string you are using is unnecessary. 

Here's a template using DBI using the exact parameter argument names and replace the text in <> with values of your DB instance (per what you had in the connection string):

> dbConnect(SQLServer(), server = <serverName>, database = <databaseName>, user = <user>, password = <password>) 

Here's a template using dplyr interface:

> src_sqlserver(server = <serverName>, database = <databaseName>, user = <user>, password = <password>)

Thanks.

Hi all,

I've got a bleeding edge extension of dplyr methods for MS SQL Server in RSQLServer. I've tested this on one of our SQL Servers and the key methods work (mostly). It's using the jTDS drivers so it should work with MS SQL Server version 8+ (i.e. MS SQL Server 2000 +). 

I would appreciate any further testing by other users of SQL Server, new issues for bugs and pull requests for any fixes / improvements. I am hoping to introduce a test harness soon.

To install:

devtools::install_github("imanuelcostigan/RSQLServer@feature/dplyr")

Thanks!
